div.head: EARLESTOWN & NEWTON.ICOUNCIL MEETING AT EARLES TOWN.
div.p: EARLESTOWN & NEWTON.ICOUNCIL MEETING AT EARLES TOWN.

P.S. A. -munesewEll --rem The usual weekly gathering of the Earlestown and District P.S.A. Society, was held in the Co- operative Hall, on Sunday afternoon. There was a good muster, and the afternoon was of a most en- joyable character,the Earlestown Orchestral Society being present and giving selections of sacred music. Vocal items were given at intervals by Mrs J Sad- worth. FORMATION OF A CHORAL CLASS AT NEWTON. On Monday evening a meeting was held at St, IPeter's Schools, Newton, for the purpose of taking into consideration the formation of a choral society. The Rev JB. Ryder presided, and there was a very fair attendance. After explaining the objects of the rneeting,a resolution was carried that a society be formed, and Mr Ryder was appointed president, with Mr Singleton as vice-president. Mr J Liptrott was appointed treasurer, and Mr Collings secretary. The following were chosen as Com- mittee :—Messrs Wilkinson and Houghton, Misses Baybut and Adams. with power to aid to their number. The class will be conducted by Mr Sharpies, of Worsley,and the first practice will takel place on Monday next in St. Peter's Schools. THE SOUTH LANCASHIRE TRAMWAYS COMPANY. At a meeting of the General Purposes Committee of the Newton Urban Council held on Monday, the 7th of January, 1901, at which Councillor W Coiling- wood presided, Mr Forvvood of the firm of Messrs F J Leslie and Co ,the solicitors to the South Lanca- shire Tramways Company, and Mr B Guiseppi (the surveyor to the Company) attended before the com- mittee with respect to the requirements of the Council as to the widening of the road leading from Southworth-road along Mill-lane to the Dietrict of Warrington (Tramway No. 2) and agreed on behalf of the Company, (a) To acquire land on the easterly side of Mill-lane from the London and North-Western Railway Arches to the entrance to Newton Park for the purpose of widening the road along which the proposed tramways will run so as to allow a distance of not less than 9ft. 6in. to inter- vene between the nearest tram rail and the outside of the footpath. (b) To apply to the Board of !rade for their consent to lay down a single line in lieu of the double line shown on the deposited plans under the:London and North-Western Railway Arch in Mill-lane, Mr Forwood also agreed on behalf of the Company to widen at their own expense the Town End Bridge at Newton-le-Willows in this dis- trict so as to secure a carriageway of the minimum width of 28ft. in addition to the 'existing width of footpaths. EARLESTOWN GOOD TRKPLARS. The usual weekly session of the Hope of Earles- town Lodge of Good Templars was held in the Co- operative Hall, Wargrave-road on Monday evening,l when a very fair attendance was presided over by Bro Thomas Cutler, C T.—Bro T Cutler gave the financial report of the New Year's social gathering' which had been very successful. The report was accepted.—Bro E Newman, S J T, reported on his recent visit to Blackpool, and tendered fraternal greetings from the " Alexandra" Lodge, which he had visited with much pleasure. Seasonable greet- ings were also received by correspondenee from friends of the Pioneer Temple and Goodwill Lodge, located at Kandy, Ceylon. This being the first session of the year, 1901,and the Jubilee year of the Order's existence, Bro J Woods, L D in appropri- ate remarks, moved. and Bro George Clarke, fl E Superintendent, in similar terms seconded, and the lodge most enthusiastically and unanimously adopted the following resolutions : "That this meeting recognises the fact that this jubilee year of the Good Templar Order finds it the greatest temperance organisation in the country and in the world—numbering as it does more than eleven thousand branches located in one hundred different countries and States ; and having an
Tr&

increasing membership of 100,000 adult and junior members within its 2,100 lodges and temples in England alone. That we rejoice that since the Order originated in New York State fifty years ago it has promulgated temperance teaching at hun- dred 3 of thousands of public meetings ; that it has administered its total abstinence pledge to many millions of parsons (about 1,500,000 being thus pledged by it in England alone during the past thirty-two years); that it has circulated scores of millions of pages of temperance literatura—and now publishes over fifty magazines and newspapers in various languages ; and that it has reclaimed tens lof thousands from intemperance, and prevented 'hundreds of thousands from ever giving way to drinking habits. That inasmuch as the Order has also by its discipline and educative influences uplifted multitudes to positions ot greater useful- ness in life,and has belted the globe with a benefi- cent girdle of sobriety and fraternity; we:reverent- ly thank Almighty God for the successes thus vouch seed ; and while dedicating ourselves anew to this great work, invite all friends of humanity to join with us in our efforts for a sober country and a sober world."—The item on the programme" A trip to London and what I saw there," was introduced by Bro. George Clarke, who was r isnonsible ; and it proved both interesting and enjoyable.—Bro. Roberts, who had been a most useful member of the " Cefn " Lodge, Wrexham, North Wales District, was heartily welcomed and accepted as an Associ- ate Member of the Lodge. ...•1110mmememe ST. HELENS.

On Monday evening, the ordinary monthly meeting o the Newton-in-Makerfield Urban District Council svaf held. Mr J W Collingwood presided and there were also present :—Messre C B F Borron, C.C., J W Emmett, J.P.. N Siddeley, W Gilmour. F J Wood. J Simps'on. Dr Patterson. W Thompson, W Beatty, E L Boat, J Fitz- gerald, Thomas Ormand, E T Evans, with C Cole (clerk), and A Bowes (surveyor). THE LATE TROOPER SWANN.

The Chairman sad before proceeding with the business it was his painful duty to refer to the death of one of the Council's late servants, Mr. S“nuel Swann, who as they wero doubtless aware, left them temporarily to serve his ceuntry as a trooper in C comnany of Lancashire Hussars in South Africa. He bad l.t them, he (the chairman) was sorry to say for ever. The would remember that the Counctireasolved to keep Mr. baann's post open until he returned but that was not to be. Trooper Swann had died nobly in the cause of his Queen and country, and it was now his (the Chairman's) pain- ful duty to move that a vote of cindolence be passed and forwarded to Mr. Swann's father and relatives. The members signified their approval b 7 standing. TECHNICAL INqTRUCTION COMMITTEE.

At a meeting held on Monday, DecembAr I7ch, a letter wAs read from Mr T Ormand, bon secretary to the Via duct Institute Technical Instruction Committee. stating with respect to the proposed grant of about £9tl. to be made by the Lancashire County Council to the District Council, that that committee proposed to apply the grant to the purchase of apparatus, and a cupboard or cupboards for the careful preservation of such appara- tus, and also to obtain suitable desks for the students of experiment d science, together with hat, coat and um- brella stands, which had been recommended by one of 11.61. Inspectors. The minute was passed on the proposition of Dr. Patterson.

div.head: GAS COMMITTEE. INCREASE IN THE PRICE OF GAS.
div.p: GAS COMMITTEE. INCREASE IN THE PRICE OF GAS.

At a meeting of this committee the parents of the lads Wiliiaffl Bradley and John Mannion, together with the lads and P.-0. David Clarke, attended the com- mittee with respect to the breaking of street lamps in Common-road by those lads. It was resolved that no proceedings be taken for the breaking of the lamp; if the cost of the repairs be paid by the parents within one month, i.e., 3s Etd each person, Also that the sum of £2 be paid to P.-C. Clarke for giving the infor- mation, the Constable to obtain the sanction of the Chief Constable to receive the gratuity. The following report of the Gas Extensions Com- mittee was read :—The Engineer submitted to the Com- mittee a scheme prepared by him for extensions at the Gas Works, to be made during the ensuing two years. It was resolved that the Council be recommended to apply to the Local Government Board for their sanction to the borrowing of the sum of £20,000 to defray the cost of the extensiona and of the amount of capital charges which have hear paid out of revenue ; that an examination be made by an expert of the gas supplied to the district as to its purity and quality, and that the cost of such examination be paid by the Council ; that the Council be recommended to increase, fram them 31st December instant, the price of gas to be supplied to con- sumers from 21 81 per 1,000 cubic feet to 2 11d, less 61, per 1,000 cubic feet discount, if paid within one month of delivery of account, this increase being rendered necessary owing to the increased cost of production. It as resolved that the report be received and adopted after the words " 2s 8d per 1,000 cubic feet to 33 " hay- been substituted for "23 81 per 1,090 cubic feet to 24 lid," the increase to take effect from the Ist January, 1901. The Clerk reported that the Finance Committee had taken into consideration the question of the appoint- rnent of a clerk for the Gas Works and the Water Works, and had referred the matter to those Works Coinenittees. It was resolved that the Office Staff Com- mittee be requested to deal with the matter, and that thee be empowered to advertise for applications for the pot and to appoint such person as they rosy think fit. The minutes were passed. WATER COMMITTEE.

The following report of the Water Works suh-oom- mittee was read, viz. r—The Chairman reported as to th* interview which he and the Clerk had had with Mr Beilby (manager) and Mr E J George (secretary), of the firm of Messrs Richard Evans and Co' with respect to the sub-leasing of land adjoining St Helens-road for tbe purpose of the erection of a reservoir and tank, and stated that Messrs Evans and Co were willing to sub- lease to the Council certain land at an annual rent of 31 Per square yard. It was resolved that Councillor Smith he asked to eee Mr A C Leslie (agent to th 3 Right Hon Lord Newton), with the view of obtaining land. That a sample of water be obtained from the main and sent to Dr Brown for analysis.and that Professor D6.6pine be request- ed to make a bacteriological examination of the water. It was resolved that the clerk be instructed to write Messrs Richard Evans and Co. and state that the Council are prepared to pay to them an annual rent of lid per square yard for land near to St. Helens-road, for the erection of a reservoir and tank. The clerk reported that he had settled the claim made against the Council by Mr T Hewitt for injury to horse. on payment of the sum of £l6 in full discharge of such claim. The clerk reported that the Finance Committee had taken into consideration the question of the appointment of a clerk for the gas works and the water works,and had referred the matter to those Works Committees. Ii was rerielves that the Office Staff Committee be requested to deal with the matter, and that they be empowered to advertise for applications; for the post, and to appoint such person as they mac, think fit. A letter was read from Messrs Richard Evans and Co., Limited, applying for the per- , mission of the Council to take its water for ths supply of three houses off Acacia-street, Crow-lane. It was resolved that the application of Messrs R Evans and Co. he granted. A letter was also read from the Secretary of the Industrial Co-operative Society, Limited, stating that a water meter had been fixed on their premises without any authority, and that as the meter was not for their use they asked for the payment to them of a nominal rent of 21 61 per annum for the privilete. It was resolved that the clerk write to the secretary of the Society and inform him that the Water Works Engineer states that the meter was fixed with his (the secretary's) sanction and approval, and that therefore there must be a miannderstanding in the matter. HIGHWAYS AND SANITARY COMMITTEE. APPOINTMENT OF AN INSPECTOR.

At a meeting of this committee a letter was read from the Surveyor (Mr A Bowes) asking the committee to appoints youth to assist him in office work and in out- side surveying and levelling. It WAR resolved that the matter be referred to the Office Staff Committee.—Tho Chairman reported that he had considered the tenders received for the simply of spades and broom during the year ending the 30th September. 1901, and that he had accepted the tenders of Messrs H J Swift and Co —The Clerk reported fully with respect to the encroachment on Newton Common, and to the information which he had obtained with respect to the rights of Commoners in the Disteict It was resolved that the Clerk he instructed to submit the whole matter to the solicitors to the Com- mons Preservation Society for their opinion and advice thereof. The Clerk road a letter whieh he had received from the Secretary to the Local Government Board, drawing the attention of the Council to the powers which they I possessed under the Sale of Food and Drugs Acts of purchasing and submitting samples of beer and articles of ford to the Public Analyst for analysis. The period of twelve months for which the Inspector of nuisances and toll collector was appointed expiring on the 23rd January, 1901, it was resolved that the Clerk be in- structed to advertise for applications for, the appoint- ment of Inspector of Nuisances, the commencing salary of the officer appointed to be at the rate Of gloo per annum, niatn, to £1213 per annum. Candidates to he members of the Sanitary Institute or prepared to qualify within twelve months of the date of his appointment. the collection of the tolls, both for market and street hawking, to be done by the Inspector of Nuisances. _ .

At a further me time of the Committee held on Mon- day afternoon last, the report of the Sanitary Sub-Com- mittee with respect to the appointment of an inspector of nuisances was submitted, and it was recommended that Mr. Tlanry Ashcroft, of Golborne, be appointe4 inspector of nuisances for one year at a salary of RICO per annum, risine to £l2O per annum, subject to the sanetinn of the Local Govornment Board, and that it be claimed out of the County Fund. The Chrirman moved, and Mr Gilmour seconded the adoption of the minutes, which were ReTtlnfl to. THE TRAMWAYS EXTENSIONS. _ . . _ _

_ At the Congregational Church, St. Helens, on Monday morning, Mr. Andrew Valentine, only son of the late John Valentine, of Aberdeen, was married to Miss Mary Ann Harwood, only daurrhter of the late Mr. Ralph Har- wood, of St. Helene. Mr Valentine was formerly in the Liberal offioea of the Southport Division, but has been about two years at St. Helens. The bride has been for many years a prominent worker in connection with the Women's Liberal Alsociation movement at St. Helens. The ceremony was performed by the Rev. F W Clark') and was of a quiet description, THE HAYDOCIE COLLIERY FATALITY. On Monday morning, at the Wagon Hot, it Haydeck. Mr S Brighouse continued the inqnest on the body or John Lacy, of tation-roafi, Haydork. who was killrd at the Wood-pit, belonging to Messrs R Evans and Co., on December 29th. Several witnesses were called, all agree- ing that there was no crowding on Vila particular neon,. sion, although there had been on other days. Three men who bad worked in the pit several years said they did not remember the cage ever having missed the catches during the winding up of men before that time.—Mr Hall said it was the opinion. of expert engine winders that if _ .

Sankey the winder had stop- teed the cage two feet below the catches be had done as much as he could ha axoected to do.—The jury returned a verdict of " Accidental death," and recommended that in order to prevent crowding, a barrier be provided ar thn bettom of the shaft en that only one " winding" of men could he allowed through at once.

div.head: SAD DEATH OF THE NEWTON GAS AND WATER ENGINEER. Found in the Bath.
div.p: SAD DEATH OF THE NEWTON GAS AND WATER ENGINEER. Found in the Bath.

lkit.ch consternation was caused in Newton, on Sunday morning, by the circulation of a report, which unfortunately proved only too true, that David Henry Lloyd, the Gas and Water Engineer, to the Newton Urban District Council had been found deal in his bath, at his residence Park-road, Newton. Mr. Lloyd had been working in his office at the Gas Works, later than usual on Saturday afternoon. He arrived home somewhere about 11 o'clock,and his wife shortly afterwards went to bed leaving him sitting up with a neighbour named Em- mett About three or four o'clock on Sunday morn- ing %Ire Lloyd awoke, and hearing'water running in the bathroom, concluded her husband was having a bath, and took no further notice. She went to sleep again and did not wake until about eight o'cleck. and hearing the water still running in the bathroom , she got up and opened the bathroom door, when she was horrified to find her husband in the water, quite dead She at once called for assis- tance and sent for Dr. Watkins, who after examina- tion, gave it as his opinion that Mr. Lloyd had been dead some hours. It appears it was a cus- tomary thing for the deceased to have a bath before retiring to bed, and this fact accounts for Ifrs. Lloyd taking no notice of the running water. The deceased had held the position of Gas and Water Engineer of Newton for about two years, he heving prior to that been Assistant Gas and Water Engineer to the Wallasey Urban District Council. It was at first thought the case was one of suicide, but the absence of motive, and the testimony of the medical man disposed of that theory. The I,:nqu est. The Dangers of Geyser Lamps. Mr. Brighouse, Coroner, held an inquiry into the circumstances at the Police Buildings, Newton, on Tuesday evening. Eleanor Kate Lloyd said deceased was her hus- band. He was 35 years of age and had acted for the pas; two years as Gas and Water Engineer to the Newton-in-Makerfield Urban District Council. Deceased was a healthy man. He got home about 11. o'clock on the evening of the sth inst and com- menced playing with the children. Hearing one of the children crying in bed, she went upstairs to see what was the matter with it. Soon afterwards she went to bed leaving deceased with a friend named Emmett. She awoke about three'o'clock in the morning and heard the bathroom tap dripping and immediately concluded that her husband was hav- ing a bath as was his custom. She was so used to hearing him having a bath at that hour that she , did not take much notice of the dripping of the tap and was very soon asleep again. She awoke again at ' about a quarter to eight and hearing the bathroom tap still dripping, she went to stop it and on open- ing the door found deceased lying on his back in the bath, dead. She went out for a neighbour and at the same time sent for Dr Watkins.—Questioned by the Coroner, witness said that the bathroom window was opened a little when she went in. She did not know who had opened it. On going into the room she noticed a noxious odour of the fumes from a Geyser lamp, which was used for heating the water in the bath. A month or two ago she had to call the doctor in to two of her chil- dren who had been rendered unconscious in the bath by the fumes emanating from the lamp. She had not the slightest cause for suspecting that deceased had intended doing anything to himself. He had not been at all peculiar in his ways. Frederick James Emmett, of Park-road, Newton- le-Willows, said he was an engineer in the employ of the L. and N.-W.Railway Company at the Wagon Works at Earlestown. He was with the deceased at his residence at 11 o'clock on Saturday night. Ile sat with him in the sitting-room talking about various matters for about five minutes. When be left him, deceased seemed to be in perfect health and spirits, and on going out he opened the door for him and called out "Good night Police Constable Powell said that he received information at about 8.15 on Sunday morning and on going to the house of the deceased he found him lying on his back with his face just above the water. His head was across the room from the heating apparattis. He did not perceive any noxious fumes when he entered the room, beyond a slight smell of burning. Dr. H. Watkins said that he was called in to see the body of the deceased on the 6th and he made an examination of it. On Sunday soon after 9 a.m. he saw the body of the deceased and it was then lying on the bed. The face was placid, but the hands were clenched The right forearm was pertly bent, and the body was lying on the back. He made a post- mortem examination on Monday. Discolouration was already well marked. Ile was of opinion that, death was violent, and due to syncope, acid en failure of the heart, and partial asphyxia from drowning. The foreman of the jury asked how could deceaeed be drowned, if his head had not been in the water. Dr Watkins said the struggle for life would draw the face above the water. The body was in such a position as to indicate that a struggle had taken place. A verdict in accor line. with the medical testi- mony wag given, and the jury conveyed their sincere regret tn Mee Lloyd. Deceased he left five young children. REFERENCE AT T9E COUNCIL MEETING. At the mee,see of the Newton-in-Makerield Urban District Couneil hnld at Herieerneon on Monday evening, reference was made to the sudden death of Mr Lloyd, The ChMrman (Mr J W CnltinTnervid) feelingly alluded to the sad eeent, and said he was sure the news of Mr Lloyd's death came as a greet shock to all of them. Mr Llevd vest; in the znnith of his strength, and they hed all hoped he would have been with them for many years to come. Re had carried out a very important work in that district in a very successful manner. The inauguration of the water scheme and other duties which had devolved upon Mr Lloyd had been performed in a satisfactory war. The Chairman then proposed that a vote of condolence be passed with the widow and children. The members passed the resolution by standing.
